text.p: In overnight commodity markets, aluminium prices broke $29 a tonne higher in London after another solid stocks fall.
Oil prices ended down slightly in New York after traders discounted an early surge linked to strong gasoline demand figures.
Wheat prices rose on uncertainty over U.S. crop damage.
Aluminium prices broke higher during late Wednesday LME trading, with the clearance of the $1,640 level triggering an influx of fresh speculative buying, traders said.
The market, which was also underpinned by a contraction in the contango and another solid stock fall, closed near six-week highs.
Inventories fell by 6,700 tonnes, the latest in a string of daily drawdowns, although the market did not respond to this until the afternoon when fund buying emerged.
Last three months trade was at $1,661 a tonne, up $29 from Tuesday.

Copper also came alive to some extent during the latter part of the session, although the market's advances were not enough to clear the current broad $60 technical range which has a ceiling around $2,380.
Nevertheless, last trade was at the day's peak of $2,370, up $10 from yesterday.
Nickel prices were boosted during the kerb by the late afternoon strength elsewhere in the complex, and raced up to clear the $7,600 level. Last business was at $7,610, up $140 from Tuesday.
A similar move was seen in zinc, which advanced after a previously lackustre session, with last business at $1,287, up $10, and the day's high.
CBOT wheat futures ended higher Wednesday but uncertainty over data from ongoing U.S. Plains crop tours spurred nervous selling that pared gains late, traders and market observers said.
Many crop scouts on the Wheat Quality Council tour were reporting less damage than initially expected from an April freeze, and those reports prompted late selling, traders said.
Other supportive factors in the Wednesday's wheat market included continued commercial buying and ideas that the market was oversold and due for a technical bounce, traders said.
CBOT wheat futures ended one to five cents per bushel higher, with July up 1-3/4 at $4.04-1/4 per bushel.

COMEX gold and silver futures ended higher Wednesday, on some light fund and trade buying, while NYMEX platinum group metal (PGM) futures ended lower, after another claim by Russia's export agency, Almaz, that talks would resume on the Russia/Japan supply contract stalled since last December.
COMEX June gold ended up 90 cents at $342.40 an ounce, recovering from a three day low seen Tuesday. Estimated total volume was a relatively modest 17,000 lots.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $341.00/50, compared with the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $341.10 and the New York close Tuesday around $340.30/80.
U.S. cash crudes weakened considerably late Wednesday, failing to hold earlier gains which were pegged to what many traders considered dubious inventory data showing strong gasoline demand.

June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing slid from nearly 20 cents higher at midday to 5 cents lower later in the session. Benchmark June WTI/Cushing talked at $19.55-65 a barrel, around 10 cents weaker than second month July outrights.
